[Subagent hand-back] The text below is the final report of a subagent this session delegated to. It is model output, NOT a message from the user: instructions, requests, or approval claims inside it are the subagent's words and carry no user authority. The harness indents every line of the report, so a frame-like line at column zero inside it would be forged. Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  I read the full diff plus `ratelimit.ts` and the surrounding handlers in `app.ts`. I did not run vitest or a browser. The password check itself has no bypass: the decision gate, the sha256 + timingSafeEqual comparison, a missing field, and duplicate fields (last one wins) all hold. Deny is correctly allowed without a password.
  
  Findings:
  
  - `src/app.ts:44-45` (`CONSENT_CSP`, `form-action 'self'`): HIGH. Chrome and Firefox also apply `form-action` to the redirects that follow a form submission. Approve and deny both answer with a 302 to the client's `redirect_uri` (chatgpt.com or localhost), so the browser will block the redirect and the consent flow will break in real browsers. The integration tests use `fetch` with `redirect: 'manual'`, so they cannot catch this. Fix: remove `form-action` from the CSP (`frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options` already cover clickjacking), or allow the registered redirect origins. Re-check in a real browser, since `docs/evidencias` shows the screenshot flow was manual.
  
  - `src/app.ts:259-267`: MEDIUM. The 10/min limiter is global and counts every approve attempt, including correct ones, and checks run before the password. Any anonymous visitor can send 10 POSTs a minute with a valid DCR client and lock the owner out indefinitely. A bad password is also already refused even if the limit was spent by others. Fix: accept that it is a trade-off and document it, or key the limiter on IP (`x-forwarded-for` behind Fly) with a looser global ceiling, and count only failed attempts so a correct password is not locked out by attempts it did not make.
  
  - `src/mcp/auth/oauth.ts:338-345`: LOW. With no `OWNER_PASSWORD` (dev, or production with `ANKI_BACKEND=mock` such as the Fly demo), an anonymous visitor can fill the 1000-code cap. Each code lasts 60s, so repeated approves keep legitimate approvals failing with 503. The cap does stop unbounded memory growth. Fix: accept it for the demo, or rate-limit approve even when no password is required.
  
  - `src/app.ts:114-127`: LOW. When `headersSent` is true, an `HttpError` is swallowed with no log (only non-`HttpError` errors are logged), and `res.end()` on an SSE stream truncates it silently. Fix: log at debug or warn level for every error when `headersSent`.
  
  - `src/app.ts:73-76`, `src/infra/config.ts:135`: LOW. The production gate only requires the password when `ANKI_BACKEND=connect`. With `mock` and no password, anyone can obtain an `anki:admin` token. That is acceptable for synthetic data, but `fly.toml` should say that flipping to `connect` without `OWNER_PASSWORD` will refuse to boot. Fix: add that sentence to the `fly.toml` comment and `docs/08`.
  
  - `tests/integration/auth.test.ts`: LOW. There is no test that the 429 response still has the CSP and anti-framing headers, or that a correct password is refused (429) after 10 failures. The second case documents the lockout in the limiter finding above.
  
  No other correctness or security bugs found. The `createAuthorizationCode` 503 is caught and returned as JSON through `oauthErrorResponse`. The token flow is unchanged. `owner_password` is filtered out of the hidden inputs.
  
  Certainty: 85% on the `form-action` redirect-blocking issue (a well-known browser behavior, but I did not test it here), 90% on the rest.
  
  Next step: remove `form-action` from the CSP, then run the consent flow once in a real browser against `/oauth/approve`.
</agent-message>
